To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the antioxidant blend was not as effective in reducing aflatoxicosis in growing-finishing pigs as was the hydrated sodium calcium alumninum silicate (HSCAS) agent.

the addition of HSCAS and antioxidants to diets containing AB1 reduced aflatoxin-induced alterations in feed intake and growth performance, and reduced the concentrations of aflatoxin in the serum, liver, and kidney, and the concentration of aflatoxin-DNA adducts in the liver.
HSCAS and antioxidant supplementation were both efficacious in mitigating the adverse effects of aflatoxin on growth performance and feed efficiency in weaned pigs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of HSCAS to bind aflatoxin and reduce its toxicity in swine.
the development of new methods of analysis for the determination of aflatoxins in food and feed.
the development and evaluation of new technologies to reduce aflatoxin contamination in food and feed.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HSCAS and antioxidants used in this study were effective in mitigating the adverse effects of AB1 on pig performance and physiological parameters.

the addition of HSCAS and/or the antioxidant preparation to a diet contaminated with 500 ppb AB1 resulted in a significant reduction in feed intake, weight gain, and serum concentrations of AB1 and aflatoxin M1 (AFM1) compared to the diet contaminated with 100 ppb AB1.
HSCAS is effective in reducing the toxicity of aflatoxin in pigs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the antioxidant blend and HSCAS were effective in reducing the effects of AB1 in the pig model, and that the effects of the antioxidants were additive to those of HSCAS.
the antioxidant blend was not as effective as the HSCAS in reducing the effects of the aflatoxin on the animals.
the HSCAS and antioxidant blend were effective in mitigating the effects of AFB1.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we need to understand how to use the information we have on these agents to develop a more complete understanding of their potential benefits and risks, and to determine the best ways to incorporate them into the diets of animals and people.

we have shown that the HSCAS and antioxidant preparation are able to mitigate the effects of aflatoxin in pigs, but the antioxidant preparation is not able to protect the pigs from the effects of aflotoxin on their immune response.
